summary: Describes using the Generic Associated Channel Label in pseudowires in MPLS Transport Profile networks. It updates RFC 5586 by removing a restriction on using that label for pseudowires. It is a standards-track document.

eli5.summary: Some network messages are about the network itself rather than customer data. A special label marks those. This lifts a rule that kept the label off certain tunnels.

questions: can gal be used with pseudowires
what does rfc 6423 change in rfc 5586
subtitle: Lets the Generic Associated Channel Label be used with pseudowires in MPLS-TP, removing a restriction from RFC 5586.

tldr.problem: RFC 5586 said the GAL MUST NOT be used with pseudowires in MPLS-TP, while placing no such restriction in other MPLS environments.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 6423 replaces that text so the GAL MAY be used with pseudowires, and says its presence means an ACH immediately follows the MPLS label stack.
tldr.outcome: The GAL can be used on a G-ACh for LSPs, Concatenated Segments of LSPs, Sections and PWs in both MPLS and MPLS-TP without discrimination.

today: RFC 6423 is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 5586. No later RFC obsoletes it.

sections.title: Background
sections.content:
RFC 5586 generalizes the Associated Channel mechanism of RFC 5085 for use with Sections, Label Switched Paths (LSPs) and Pseudowires (PWs) in MPLS networks. The Associated Channel Header (ACH) is generalized as the Generic Associated Channel (G-ACh).

RFC 5586 also defines a label-based exception mechanism, the Generic Associated Channel Label (GAL), that works with the ACH for LSPs, but it prohibits GAL usage with PWs in MPLS-TP.
sections.eli5: Some tunnels carry special messages about the network itself. A special label flags those messages, but an older rule banned that label on one kind of tunnel.

sections.title: The Inconsistency and the Fix
sections.content:
RFC 5586 Section 4.2 says that in MPLS-TP the GAL MUST be used on a G-ACh on LSPs, Concatenated Segments of LSPs and Sections, and MUST NOT be used with PWs. Yet in other MPLS environments it places no restriction on using the GAL with PWs.

That inconsistency may cause unnecessary implementation differences and disagrees with the MPLS-TP requirements in RFC 5654. RFC 6423 therefore specifies that the GAL can be used with LSPs, Concatenated Segments of LSPs, Sections and PWs in both MPLS and MPLS-TP environments without discrimination.
sections.eli5: The old rule treated one kind of tunnel differently depending on where it was used. That caused confusion, so now the same rule applies everywhere.

sections.title: Text Replaced in RFC 5586
sections.content:
In the Introduction of RFC 5586, the sentence about the GAL working with the ACH for LSPs and MPLS Sections is extended with "and for PWs".

In Section 4.2, the rule becomes: in MPLS-TP, the GAL MUST be used on a G-ACh on LSPs, Concatenated Segments of LSPs and Sections, and MAY be used with PWs. The presence of a GAL indicates that an ACH immediately follows the MPLS label stack.

The security section says there are no further security considerations than those in RFC 5586.
sections.eli5: Two sentences in the old document were rewritten. The ban on pseudowires became a permission, and the label still tells you a special header comes next.
